headline: Proforma revenue grew 63% and PAT 52% in FY26 with cash tax paid, but operating cash flow was 8.6% of PAT, the audited history is a pre-acquisition shell until FY26, and the Rs 3,000 m raise funds working capital and an 8x expansion of one plant.
red_flags: Proforma revenue +63.1% and PAT +51.7% in FY26 (Rs 4,139.70 m, Rs 313.90 m); EBITDA margin 13.46% vs 14.51% proforma FY25
FY26 operating cash flow Rs 26.85 m = 8.6% of PAT; inventory +Rs 445.46 m
Cash tax: current tax 29.3% of FY26 PBT; direct tax paid Rs 104.52 m
Top customer Seth Agro 25.21% and top 10 customers 50.04% of FY26 revenue; dealers, no long-term contracts
Rs 1,100 m of a Rs 3,000 m raise funds working capital; Rs 716.64 m expands Dehlon from 4,000 to 33,000 units on land leased from a promoter
Borrowings Rs 1,344.07 m (D/E 1.89x); Rs 1,340.89 m covered by promoter personal guarantees
reference_note: Rs 158.47 = 28.10x (arithmetic average P/E of the issuer's three listed peers, p. 155) x FY26 basic EPS Rs 5.64 (p. 154). A mechanical reference built from the issuer's own peer table, not a price band; the only primary issue (Oct-2025, for the acquired businesses) was at a bonus- and split-adjusted Rs 35.15 and is not a market price (pp. 163-164).

strengths: Proforma revenue Rs 2,074.48 m to Rs 2,537.60 m to Rs 4,139.70 m, FY24-FY26 (pp. 87, 92)
ROCE 31.10% and interest cover 5.03x in FY26 (p. 158)
Current tax 29.3% of FY26 PBT, so profit is taxed in cash (p. 87)
Top 10 suppliers only 40.53% of FY26 purchases (p. 33)
Utilisation at Dehlon 89.68% and Cheema 73.62% in FY26 (p. 267)
weaknesses: FY26 CFO Rs 26.85 m vs PAT Rs 313.90 m (p. 88)
Top customer 25.21%, top 10 customers 50.04% of FY26 revenue (p. 36)
FY24-FY25 audited history is the pre-acquisition company (p. 19)
Promoters have limited formal education and no listed-company board experience (p. 48)
opportunities: Domestic farm-equipment market projected at 7.7% CAGR FY26-FY30, issuer-commissioned CARE report (p. 129)
Organised makers hold about 60% of implements and are expected to gain share (p. 221)
threats: Subsidy schemes (60% Central, 40% State) can be reduced or withdrawn (p. 56)
Punjab 25.79% and Haryana 18.48% of FY26 revenue: monsoon and policy concentration (p. 56)
Rs 945.02 m of Rs 1,150 m working-capital limits drawn at 31-Aug-2026 (p. 42)

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -52.1% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess
model.reverse_dcf: Current free cash flow is negative: no multiple can be stated, and the entire price rests on a turn that has not yet begun.
